decay.predictor_vs_target: SAME family as base: base's own predictor, started from base's exact weights, pulled back toward them

fast.predictor_vs_target: SAME family as base: base's own predictor (obs→256→256→64 ReLU MLP, one layer deeper than the obs→256→64 target), started from base's exact weights

feat.predictor_vs_target: SAME family as base, over value_pooled: target D→256→64, predictor D→256→256→64 (D = D_MODEL), its own frozen target and its own feature normalisation
feat.why: the trunk-feature input, live: measures the representation drift the offline read predicted

small.predictor_vs_target: DELIBERATELY LESS EXPRESSIVE than the target: obs→32→64 (one hidden layer of 32) against the target's 256 hidden units, so it cannot represent the target exactly
small.why: no fingerprinting: too little capacity to memorise battles; novelty tracks coarse density

e_identification.rule: INDETERMINATE iff f_i > 0.7; else IDENTIFIES iff Holm (across the keys) rejects S <= 0.5 (one-sided); SELECTIVE iff Holm rejects S >= 0.5; else UNDECIDED. `verdict_unadjusted` is the per-key 95 % CI rule, reported only. S = log f_ii / log f_i: 0 = learns only what it visits, 1 = identifies the target everywhere
